author: buchanan_robert
text:
The sea is calm, and wide, and deep ;

The white foam dies away from me :

My heart is still, but not at rest :

For something waits for me afar.

author: cushag
text:
In de'er fields, where summer bees

Are busy at their toil,
Among the clover-blossoms thin

I sit and dream awhile;
For dreams I love them better far

Than work can give to man,
And as my eyes are heavy soon

My eyelids close again.

Tuk Tuk, tuk-tuk, tuk tuk! The driver is going to stop! I must jump out of this moving vehicle and get home safe. author: emily_dickinson
text: This is a verse that was written by William Cullen Bryant as he looked out at his farm on a hot summer day, so this has always been my favorite poem. It’s very simple; it almost reminds me of an old rhyme or children’s song from back in the 1920’s. The language used gives off such a relaxed tone. Also, this poem is not difficult to follow. My thoughts are drawn into the peaceful scene of a beautiful rural setting.

text:
And yet he knows not what is coming to him,
How his heart will break; how bitter life will be,

When all is over and the glory fled from him ;
Nor cares about it—or if he does, but feigns
To do so, lest some one should pity him.

author: john_masefield
text:
On that day I knew you were mine,

And you smiled and said: "I guess so,"
But your eyes were kind with an old-time shine,

Like the glow in a winter sunset;
Then your hair was black as ebony,

Your face fair as a maiden's dream;
And I felt my soul grow more serene—

You had made me happy, 'Neath Heaven!

author: john_keats
text:
The golden sun casts its rays on the rocky mountain peak,
But no sound is heard as if all life has ceased.
Not even a bee's hum or an eagle's cry can be heard,
For it seems like time stands still here.

I walk through these silent hallways,
As I follow the footsteps of those who have come before me.
Each step feels heavy, as if carrying their own burdens;
Yet they keep walking forward without looking back.

This journey leads me deeper into my past;
To remember every moment spent with friends forgotten—or lost

author: john_keats
john_masefield
text:
I think I know you now; you're very good,
You have done nothing wrong or unkind

To anyone who cares to see your face

For I never knew such beauty since I came —

Your eyes are dark and full of flame!

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
He saw her standing there, as white and clean as snow;
And his heart was crying for joy to see her once more.

The wind blew from the east, cold with winter's breath,
When he came to the house where she lived alone that day:
But when she looked at him with eyes full of gladness,
Her cheeks were warm and red like fire in burning clay.

Tibetan monks are masters of concentration, being able to meditate for hours without moving or talking. The practice is called samadhi and it requires years of dedication and training. It’s very important that they don’t move their bodies or talk while meditating, because even slight movement can disturb the mind and throw off the focus required for the meditation.

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
I am too old for this world. . ..
And it was time to sail across the vast ocean
Of sorrow, loneliness, fear. .
But there were so many tears on my face. . ,

The wind took me away from land. . And brought
me here. . ... To live in my own boat. .

How happy I was with the open sea. . !
To feel how warm water embraces me. . ....

There is no one here to disturb me.

text:

 So much as life to thee appears;
 The golden hours are past for ever,

 And all that love and pride can do
 Can add but pleasure to thy power.’

author: robert_frost
text:
The sea is a sailor’s home,
Where he goes to be cool and calm;

He does not fear nor dread,
A storm or an angry gale,

But if one should chance to come,
Then he sits tight by his helm,

And when it has passed away,
He whistles his song again

text:
Oh poor man, you have no luck! All your life,
you've had to endure great pain. You are always hungry,
and yet you work like a slave for some petty lord who
gives you little to eat. But why complain when even
Alexander the Great himself suffered much more than
you did?

author: newman_john_henry_1801_1890
robert_frost
text:
A-I-N, I knew you for an hour or so,
And now my head is aching with your go;

You were all wrong and said you would be right,
So that was what you meant when you smiled so sweet;

And then I kissed you on the cheek and left you,
Not knowing how it hurt me to part from you—

But though we parted far away from here,
We’re still together as we always are!

 Another world awaits us ; when God spoke,
 The world was made ; and He, who formed it so,
 Made man to be His servant— made him free.

 Our life here leads from woe unto joy;
 For evil brings with it good at last —
 A day of hope will come for every cast!

author: stothert_james_a
text:
O! this magnet which draws us together,
This universal power that stirs our souls;
It whispers secrets hidden in nature,

Unravels mysteries long shrouded in goals.
Its gentle embrace, like cosmic energy,

Breaks down barriers separating space and time,
Connecting hearts across oceans vast,

Merging minds that once were apart from thine.

author: thomas_hardy
text:
And when the night was black and cold,

 And all my dreams were dark and old,

 It seemed that something from below

 Was drawing me across the snow ;

 My soul was sore with pain and woe,

 Till I looked up into his face;

 The pale white light upon his brow

 Made it as bright as silver lace:

 For I had found the Way to go

 To Christ the Lord who died for me !

author: william_wordsworth
text: The stars are an integral part of our existence. They have been a source of wonder for us from time immemorial. We have always looked up at them, wondered about their origin and existence, and tried to decipher the meaning behind all these mysteries. The ancient Greeks gave names to each star based on its position and role in our lives. From time to time we look at the stars and try to understand what they signify. Sometimes, when everything seems to be falling apart, we find solace in looking at those twinkling points above us. It gives us hope and courage.
